lessons.title: Too … to → So … that
lessons.content: Sentences using 'too … to' can be transformed into 'so … that' sentences. 'Too + adjective + to + V1' becomes 'so + adjective + that + cannot/could not + V1'. For different subjects, 'too + adj + for person + to + V1' becomes 'so + adj + that + person + cannot/could not + V1'.

details.explanation: Replace 'too' with 'so' and add 'that … cannot/could not' before the verb.
details.example: He is too proud to beg. → He is so proud that he cannot beg.
details.burmese: သူက အရမ်းမာနကြီးလို့ မတောင်းနိုင်ဘူး။

details.explanation: Move the 'for person' part after 'that' as the subject of the result clause.
details.example: The bag was too heavy for me to lift. → The bag was so heavy that I could not lift it.
details.burmese: အိတ်က ငါအတွက် မမော့နိုင်လောက်အောင် လေးတယ်။

lessons.title: So … that → Too … to
lessons.content: Sentences using 'so … that' can be transformed into 'too … to' sentences. 'So + adjective + that + cannot/could not + V1' becomes 'too + adjective + to + V1'. When the result clause has a different subject, use 'too + adj + for person + to + V1'.

details.explanation: Remove 'that cannot/could not' and replace 'so' with 'too'.
details.example: This exercise is so difficult that I cannot do it. → This exercise is too difficult for me to do.
details.burmese: ဒီအားကစားက ငါလုပ်လို့မရနိုင်လောက်အောင် ခက်တယ်။

details.explanation: The subject of the 'that' clause becomes 'for + person' in the 'too … to' form.
details.example: There are so many birds that I cannot count them. → There are too many birds for me to count.
details.burmese: ငါရေတွက်လို့မရနိုင်လောက်အောင် ငှက်တွေ အများကြီးရှိတယ်။
